notes: Phase 1 rich-club coefficient sequence via src/algorithms/properties/rich_club.rs. The algorithm is strictly O(|V| + |E|) with three linear passes: (1) invert vertex_order into order_of[v] in O(|V|), (2) bucket each edge into res[min(order_of[v1], order_of[v2])] in O(|E|), (3) reverse cumulative sweep plus optional per-step normalization in O(|V|). Karate (34v / 78e) at 336 ns is dominated by the bucket fill loop and the |V|-length sum; grid-30x30 (900v / 1740e) at 5.6 µs scales mostly with |V| since per-edge work is cheap and constant. The gnp(1000, p=0.05) sample (~25k edges) at 34 µs confirms linear-in-|E| growth: the karate→gnp jump is ~100× the runtime for ~320× the edges, with the difference explained by sub-µs constant per-call overhead amortizing out on the larger run. python-igraph 0.11.9 does not expose rich_club_sequence (no binding generated for it) so no cross-language comparison; the upstream C reference reports correctness only via .out fixtures, no timings.
